(BY SHRI ARPAN SHRIVASTAVA - ADVOCATE FOR THE APPELLANTS  (BY MS. GUNJAN NAIK - ADVOCATE FOR THE RESPONDENT NO.3   _________________________________________________________  This appeal coming on for admission this day, the court   following:
 ORDER
As in the instant case, liability to pay the compensation is not disputed.
Hence, there is no need to serve respondent No.2.
With the consent of both learned counsel for the parties, heard finally at motion stage.

2. This appeal has been filed by the claimant/appellant under Section 173 (1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 against the award dated 27.08.2019 passed in MACC.No.213 of 2019 by the Member of VIIIth additional MACT, Sagar District- Sagar, seeking enhancement of compensation.
3. Learned counsel for the appellants submits that Tribunal has not determined deceased's income appropriately.
It should have been determined on the basis of minimum wages.
On above ground, it is urged that compensation awarded by the Tribunal be suitably enhanced.
4. Learned counsel for respondent/Insurance Company submits that compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and proper and no enhancement is required.

5. I have heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused record of the case.
6. So far as income of deceased is concerned, on the date of accident, minimum wages of an unskilled labour were Rs.7,375/-.
On the date of accident, deceased was aged 23 years.

Therefore,
40% is to be added as future prospects and multiplier of 18 is to be applied.
As deceased was Bachelor.
Therefore, one half is to be deducted for personal and living expenses.
Appellants being parents of deceased
, are entitled to receive Rs.40,000/- each for consortium.
Further, appellants are entitled to receive Rs.15,000/- for loss of estate and Rs.15,000/- for funeral expenses.

7. Hence, in view of above, compensation awarded by Tribunal is recalculated as under:-
 S.No. Heads   1.

Monthly Income of the deceased   2. Added Future Prospects 40% 
 3. Personal & Living Expenses of the deceased  (1/2)
 4. Monthly loss of dependency   5. Annual loss of dependency   7. Total loss of dependency  8. Compensation for loss of estate and funeral Rs.30,000/-
expenses 9.

Compensation for loss of spousal/parental/filial Rs.80,000/-
consortium 10

Total Compensation Rs.12,24,992/-
11.

Total compensation awarded by the Tribunal Rs.7,50,400/-
12.

Actual enhancement Rs.4,74,592/-
8.

Hence, compensation awarded by the Tribunal is enhanced by Rs.4,74,592/-
9.
So far as issue of confining enhancement of compensation to the extent Court fees is paid, in this Court's opinion, in view of law laid down by Hon'ble Apex Court in Kavita Banukila & Ors.

Vs.
Santosh Kumar Vs. Santosh Kumar & Anr in Civil Appeal No.8053 of 2024, enhancement of compensation cannot be restricted to the extent Court fees is paid.
